3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The phone started ringing. I took a deep breath as I held it to my ear.

5.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
5.text: “Mr. Rayne. How pleasing it is to finally get a chance to speak with you in person. ”

7.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
7.text: “I am Queen Beatrice Livingston. The Queen of the Four Corners of Merkopa, Defender of Castle Tzarsbourgh, Conqueror of the Tranquil Sea, Stout Protector of the Ancient Lands of Rum, Descendant of the Most Honorable King Edward the First and the Ruler of Rumburg. ”

9.speaker: Player
9.text: “It is very nice to finally talk to you as well.”

10.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
10.text: “I am afraid protocol must be observed.”

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: I was in my office, waiting for the call that could potentially change the future of Eastern Merkopa.

14.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
14.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_FPnT_Consulate_Condemn"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_JointOperation"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn09_RumburgPeaceSummit_StartTalks"] == true) == false

17.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
17.text: “Now. I wanted to give you a call *personally* to thank you for your efforts in maintaining the peace in Eastern Merkopa.”

18.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
18.text: “The reparations Sordland paid were very well received by my people and we are forever thankful. Instead of burying the dark past, you are trying to heal the wounds.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “My aim is to have peace in Merkopa. Nothing more.”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “I decided that Sordland would benefit from better relationships with its neighbors.”

22.speaker: Player
22.text: “It was time to mend old wounds and rightfully pay for what we had done.”

23.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
23.text: “You are quite an unusual president for Sordland, Mr. Rayne.”

24.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
24.text: “I applaud and thank you from the bottom of my heart.”

25.speaker: Player
25.text: “I am hoping this will mark an end to the aggressions between our countries.”

26.speaker: Player
26.text: “This is only the beginning. We have the potential to do so much more. Don't you think so?”

28.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
28.text: “Of course. This is the beginning of a new era after all.”

32.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
32.text: “An offer that has the potential to improve the relationship between our countries once and for all.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “I don't like the sound of this.”

37.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
37.text: “Peace is very fragile and costly, but I think we are off to a good start.”

38.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
38.text: “I would like to hold a peace summit between Sordland and Rumburg.”

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “There is always a but, isn't there?”

42.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
42.text: “I can't let my people suffer in the name of peace with Sordland.”

43.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
43.text: “I must admit your country has a resource that Rumburg has long yearned for.”

46.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
46.text: “I want you to expand the Sordish natural gas pipeline to Rumburg, and I want it 30% cheaper than your other neighbors.”

47.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
47.text: “If you accept, we will give Sordland licenses to make your own version of the KA-74. It should certainly be profitable in the long term, not to mention the aid it will give to your national defense.”

48.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
48.text: “And then we will have our peace summit -- and perhaps start talking about even more lucrative deals.”

49.speaker: Player
49.text: “If you want your peace, you'll need to come up with a better deal than that.”

50.speaker: Player
50.text: “I'm afraid Sordland is not in a position to accept this deal. I must refuse.”

51.speaker: Player
51.text: “Anything in the name of peace in East Merkopa. I accept.” [-1 Government Budget]

56.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
56.text: “Mr. Rayne, you have proven yourself to be a better leader than I thought.”
56.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Media_Censored"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_Censored"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Law_MediaBias"] == true) == false)

57.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
57.text: “We have just written history on this short call.”

58.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
58.text: “My people will talk to your people, and we will make the deal official.”

61.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
61.text: “I'm afraid we are at the end of the reserved time for our call.”

62.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
62.text: “If that is all, I wish you a good afternoon.”

65.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
65.text: “I'm afraid we are at the end of the reserved time for our call.”

69.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
69.text: “I am certain that this will be the start of a lasting friendship.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “As long as Rumburg respects its boundaries.”

71.speaker: Player
71.text: “We have achieved so much in such a short span. It's been a pleasure.”

73.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
73.text: “And as long as Sordland respects its own.”

76.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
76.text: “I can't wait to meet with you in person at the peace summit. We have so much to talk about.”

77.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
77.text: “But for now, I'm afraid we are at the end of the reserved time for our call.”

79.speaker: Narrator
79.text: Was this the start of a new era?

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: Just like that, I had thrown away any chance of a peace summit between Rumburg and Sordland.

82.speaker: Narrator
82.text: Would our countries ever be able to reconcile?

84.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
84.text: “Forgive me for being so straightforward, but I have to ask.”

85.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
85.text: “Now. Given the circumstances, I never thought I would be giving you a personal phone call. Yet here we are.”
85.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn02_FPnT_Consulate_Condemn"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_JointOperation"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn09_RumburgPeaceSummit_StartTalks"] == true) == false

86.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
86.text: “Even after what Sordland has done, I am showing you my willingness to talk instead of cutting off communication.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “I did not hang up yet. That should show you *my* willingness to listen to your whining.”

90.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
90.text: “I assure you, there is no need for sarcasm, Mr. Rayne.”

92.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
92.text: “My demands are simple. You will give us control of our stolen ancestral homelands, Estord and Narbel.”

93.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
93.text: “Those cities are surely of lesser importance to you judging by the way your country has treated them. That's all I ask.”

97.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
97.text: “I know it all, Mr. Rayne. I know all about your plans. I can read your every move.”

98.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
98.text: “I know that your military is weak and crumbling.”

105.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
105.text: “I know that Sordland is on the verge of being completely under the control of your general staff.”

106.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
106.text: “I am offering you a peaceful way out of your dire situation.”
106.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.RumburgIncident_RumburgKnows"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn09_Military_WeakAgainstRumburg"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Security_Unrest_Military"] == true) == false)

107.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
107.text: “One does not have to look far to see the situation your military is in.”

111.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
111.text: “So, please. I beg you to have reason. Think of your citizens. Think of your people.”

112.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
112.text: “If you fail to comply, to put it simply, we will take them by force.”

114.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
114.text: “Do not enter a war that you have no chance of winning.”

115.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
115.text: “Please listen to me carefully. This is your last chance.”

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “You must be out of your mind if you thought I would give in to your threats.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “You dare insult me? Your time is over, Your Highness. Along with your country. I will see you on the battlefield.”

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “I will not lead my country to a war. Peace must be maintained by any means necessary.”

123.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
123.text: “I have given you a chance and you refused. You have failed your people.”

125.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
125.text: “You will regret your decision until your last breath.”

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: And just like that, the Rumburg War had begun.

128.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
128.text: “That's all. Your two least important cities.”

129.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
129.text: “I am glad that you see it our way.”

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “You must be joking. I have a duty to protect this nation. I will not sell pieces of it.”

132.speaker: Player
132.text: “What are two backwater cities in the name of peace? I accept.”

134.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
134.text: “Mr. Rayne, you have proven yourself to be a better leader than I thought.”

135.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
135.text: “You have protected your citizens and fulfilled your duty. For that, I applaud you.”

137.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
137.text: “My people will talk to your people and we will make the deal official.”

138.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
138.text: “For now, I'm afraid we are at the end of the reserved time for our call.”

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: And just like that, part of my country was now Rumburg territory.

142.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
142.text: “I understand your frustration, but you have made the better choice.”

143.speaker: Player
143.text: “You will pay for this one day.”

144.speaker: Beatrice Livingston
144.text: “No need for additional adversity at this point.”

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: I heard the voice of the Queen of Rumburg from the other side.

149.speaker: Narrator
149.text: Just like that, I had thrown away any chance of a peace summit between Rumburg and Sordland.

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: Just like that, there was about to be peace between Rumburg and Sordland.
150.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Diplomacy_Energy_PriceSurge"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Diplomacy_Energy_PriceSurge"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Diplomacy_Energy_PriceFluctuation"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Diplomacy_Energy_PriceFluctuation"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Gasom_Ownership_ForeignOwned"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Gasom_Ownership_ForeignOwned"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn03_EnT_Gasom_OnlyRiziaInvestment"] == true) == false)

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: The decision wouldn't make me popular. But it was better than the alternative.

198.speaker: Player
198.text: “Anything in the name of peace in East Merkopa. I accept.” [-2 Government Budget]

199.speaker: Player
199.text: “Anything in the name of peace in East Merkopa. I accept.” [-3 Government Budget]

213.speaker: Player
213.text: “Wait. Not so fast. I will accept your deal.” [-1 Government Budget]

214.speaker: Player
214.text: “Wait. Not so fast. I will accept your deal.” [-2 Government Budget]

215.text: “Wait. Not so fast. I will accept your deal.” [-3 Government Budget]
